sample_unit: test runs (5 models x 5 scenarios x 10 repetitions)
models_evaluated: five state-of-the-art LLMs (names not given in abstract)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on a clinical question under neutral versus misleading prompt framings
links.effect: Baseline accuracy 100% for all models; fell to 45% with incorrect self-recall prompts and 1% with authoritative prompts; Cramér's V = 0.75, P < .001.
links.quote: However, accuracy significantly decreased in conditions with misleading cues, dropping to 45% with self-recall prompts and 1% with authoritative prompts.

links.outcome: Self-rated LLM confidence when accuracy collapsed under authoritative cue
links.effect: Accuracy collapsed in the authoritative condition, but self-rated confidence stayed high with no statistical difference from baseline.
links.quote: Notably, while accuracy collapsed in the authoritative condition, the models' self-rated confidence remained high, showing no statistical difference from the baseline condition.

screen.reason: Empirical study testing the susceptibility of five LLMs to sycophancy/misleading cues (subjective impressions and authoritative cues) in clinical questions; it evaluates model vulnerability/accuracy under adversarial or noisy prompt phrasing rather than testing a deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
